record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: periods over Q for a specific quadratic Hénon map
record.original_question: Over Q, does the map (x,y)↦(y,y^2+c+x) have no rational point of exact period N except when N is one of 1,2,3,4,6,8?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3 (see [91]). — Over Q, (x, y) 7→ (y, y2 + c + x) has no point of period N, other than N ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a rational parameter $c \in \mathbb{Q}$, consider the quadratic Hénon map
$$f_c : \mathbb{A}^2 	o \mathbb{A}^2, \qquad (x, y) \mapsto (y,\; y^2 + c + x).$$
A point $P \in \mathbb{Q}^2$ is said to have exact period $N \geq 1$ under $f_c$ if $f_c^N(P) = P$ and $f_c^k(P) 
eq P$ for every $1 \leq k < N$.

Prove or disprove: for every $c \in \mathbb{Q}$ and every $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ with $N 
otin \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8\}$, the map $f_c$ has no rational point of exact period $N$.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is listed as a conjecture in a recent compilation of open problems on Hénon maps. A 2024 preprint constructs Hénon maps over $\mathbb{Q}$ with many integral periodic points and gives a quadratic lower bound for any uniform bound on rational periodic points, but does not appear to settle this particular conjecture for the quadratic family. No resolution was found in the search.
